panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a real patient clinical photo with caption explicitly describing early-stage periorificial dermatitis with perioral papules and vermilion sparing, matching vocabulary findings. B: Panel B is a real patient clinical photo with caption describing progressive periorificial dermatitis with coalescing perioral and nasolabial papules, matching vocabulary findings.
panels.attribution_text: Guarda et al. Recalcitrant Perioral Dermatitis Successfully Controlled With Low-Dose Isotretinoin: A Case Report.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.105896. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Gradual onset and progressive worsening of periorificial dermatitis (A) Early-stage presentation showing scattered monomorphic erythematous papules localized to the chin and perioral region, with relative sparing of the vermilion border and surrounding facial skin. Lesions appear small, non-pustular, and distributed in a periorificial pattern. (B) Progressive clinical worsening with increased density of erythematous papules coalescing into ill-defined plaques involving the nasolabial folds and perioral area. Background erythema and subtle superficial scaling are visible, consistent with evolving periorificial dermatitis.
in_text_mentions: r medical history was notable for erythematotelangiectatic rosacea and linear porokeratosis affecting the feet, as well as a family history of rosacea. Approximately four months after prolonged mask use during the COVID-19 pandemic, scattered erythematous papules began to develop insidiously over the chin, nasolabial folds, and periorificial areas while sparing the remainder of the face. Rather than an acute eruption, lesions evolved slowly over time, progressively increasing in number and coalescing into erythematous plaques associated with burning sensation and mild pruritus (Figure 1A, 1B).

panels.figure_caption: Clinical presentation of TOP STRIPED A 54-year-old man presenting with tender erythema on his face after applying clobetasol 0.05% cream for two months. The clinical features of his TOP STRIPED are shown (black ovals) on the frontal facial view. TOP STRIPED, topical steroid-induced perioral dermatitis
in_text_mentions: At his follow-up visit 18 months after the initial clearing of his hand dermatitis, he presented with perinasal, perioral, and malar tender erythema on his face (Figure 1 and Figure 2). During the prior two months, he had been applying the clobetasol cream once or twice daily on his face. The areas of application had been dry and were in a distribution typically affected by seborrheic dermatitis.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Real clinical photograph of a 36-year-old male showing monomorphic erythematous scaly papules localized to the periorbital area, consistent with the article's diagnosis of granulomatous periorificial dermatitis. The periocular papular eruption is a textbook location for periorificial dermatitis. [raw subtype: granulomatous] B: Real clinical photograph of the same patient showing monomorphic erythematous scaly papules localized to the paranasal and perioral areas, consistent with the article's diagnosis of granulomatous periorificial dermatitis. The caption explicitly notes involvement of the vermilion border, which is unusual for periorificial dermatitis (where a spared zone is typical), so this panel is marked atypical; the vermilion border involvement is not covered by the provided vocabulary and is listed as a proposed finding. [raw subtype: granulomatous]
panels.attribution_text: Al-Qassabi et al. Granulomatous Periorificial Dermatitis in an Adult: A case report with review of literature.. Sultan Qaboos University medical journal 2020. doi:10.18295/squmj.2020.20.01.015. CC BY-ND (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nd/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Photographs of the face of a 36-year-old male showing monomorphic erythematous scaly papules localised to (A) periorbital, (B) paranasal and perioral areas with involvement of vermilion border.
in_text_mentions: Following the reoccurrence of the papular eruption, examination showed monomorphic scaly erythematous papules localised to the perioral, paranasal and periorbital areas of the face [Figure 1]. The vermilion border was involved. There was no facial erythema or telangiectasia. There were no other skin lesions and other orifices were not involved. The rest of the physical examination was unremarkable. The differential diagnoses included periorificial dermatitis, GR, cutaneous sarcoidosis and lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei (LMDF).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: H&E of erythematous papule from granulomatous periorificial dermatitis case shows granulomas, but no vocabulary finding_key (all clinical periorificial eruptions) is visibly shown on histology; no clinical manifestation can be named from image, so excluded per rule 6. B: H&E high power showing granuloma with surrounding lymphocytic infiltrate; histologic features have no matching vocabulary finding_key for periorificial dermatitis, and no clinical eruption is visible, so excluded per rule 6.
panels.attribution_text: Al-Qassabi et al. Granulomatous Periorificial Dermatitis in an Adult: A case report with review of literature.. Sultan Qaboos University medical journal 2020. doi:10.18295/squmj.2020.20.01.015. CC BY-ND (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nd/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Haematoxylin and eosin stains at (A) ×10 magnification showing non-caseating granulomatous inflammation with some naked granulomas and (B) at ×40 magnification showing surrounding lymphocytic infiltrate.
in_text_mentions: Histopathological examination of an erythematous papule showed non-caseating naked granulomas containing histiocytes, multinucleated giant cell of Langhans type and focally surrounded lymphocytes [Figure 2]. Periadnexal and perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate was also present. Stains for fungi (i.e. periodic acid–Schiff) and acid-fast bacilli (i.e. Ziehl-Neelsen and Wade-Fite) were negative.
